mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >25 bps in 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 2% at trigger).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market is strong (UNRATE > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6% and remains there for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong demand (GDPC1 YoY growth > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% for two months signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is falling sharply (UNRATE 3-month delta > -1%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by >10% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates (RSAFS 3-month delta > 0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (unemployment falls while employment rises) by more than 0.5% over two months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising faster than GDPC1 for three months) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth outpaces GDPC1 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when monetary policy is highly expansionary (FEDFUNDS < 1%).
